paraphrase: The fourth (turīya), the Lord, unchanging and all-pervading, is capable of ending all sorrows; it is non-dual, the effulgent one among all beings.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

paraphrase: Viśva and taijasa are held to be bound by cause and effect; prājña is bound by cause only; neither (cause nor effect) exists in the fourth.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: anādimāyayā supto yadā jīvaḥ prabudhyate / ajam anidram asvapnam advaitaṃ budhyate tadā
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: When the jīva, asleep under beginningless māyā, awakens, it then realizes the unborn, sleepless, dreamless non-dual (reality).
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ / māyāmātram idaṃ dvaitam advaitaṃ paramārthataḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: If the world of plurality existed it would no doubt cease; this duality is mere māyā; non-duality is the ultimate truth.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: yuñjīta praṇave cetaḥ praṇavo brahma nirbhayam / praṇave nityayuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: One should fix the mind on Oṃ; Oṃ is the fearless Brahman; for one ever united with Oṃ there is no fear anywhere.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: devasyaiṣa svabhāvo 'yam āptakāmasya kā spṛhā
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Some say creation is for the Lord's enjoyment, others for his sport; but this is the very nature of the effulgent one — what desire could one whose desires are fulfilled have?
notes: The original gives the final line only. Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: aniścitā yathā rajjur andhakāre vikalpitā / sarpadhārādibhir bhāvais tadvad ātmā vikalpitaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: As a rope not clearly seen in the dark is imagined as a snake, a line of water and so on, so the self is imagined (as various things).
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

paraphrase: When the rope is ascertained, the imagined (snake) ceases and the rope alone remains, non-dual; so is the ascertainment of the self.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: svapnamāye yathā dṛṣṭe gandharvanagaraṃ yathā / tathā viśvam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vedānteṣu vicakṣaṇaiḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: As dream and magic are seen, and as a city of the gandharvas (in the sky) is seen, so this universe is seen by those wise in the Vedānta.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ / na mumukṣur na vai mukta ity eṣā paramārthatā
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: There is no dissolution, no origination, none bound, none striving, none seeking liberation, none liberated — this is the highest truth.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: ādāv ante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā / vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo 'vitathā iva lakṣitāḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: What does not exist at the beginning and the end does not exist in the middle either; though like the unreal, (objects) are regarded as real.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: mṛllohavisphuliṅgādyaiḥ sṛṣṭir yā coditānyathā / upāyaḥ so 'vatārāya nāsti bhedaḥ kathaṃcana
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The creation taught otherwise — through clay, iron, sparks and the like — is a means for leading (the mind to the truth); there is no difference whatever.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: ātmā hy ākāśavaj jīvair ghaṭākāśair ivoditaḥ / ghaṭādivac ca saṃghātair jātāv etan nidarśanam
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The self is like space, manifested as the jīvas as space is as the spaces in pots; as pots are compounds, so are bodies — this is the illustration of birth.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: ātmasatyānubodhena na saṅkalpayate yadā / amanastāṃ tadā yāti grāhyābhāve tadagraham
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: When, through knowing the truth of the self, the mind no longer imagines, it becomes no-mind; in the absence of anything to grasp, it grasps nothing.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: asparśayogo vai nāma durdarśaḥ sarvayogibhiḥ / yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The yoga called 'contactless' (asparśa) is hard to see for all yogins; the yogins fear it, seeing fear in the fearless.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: utseka udadher yadvat kuśāgreṇaikabindunā / manaso nigrahas tadvad bhaved aparikhedataḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Control of the mind is to be achieved without weariness, like emptying the ocean drop by drop with the tip of a kuśa grass blade.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: laye saṃbodhayec cittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ / sakaṣāyaṃ vijānīyāt samaprāptaṃ na cālayet
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: When the mind is lapsing into dullness (laya) one should rouse it; when distracted, calm it again; when it has latent impressions (kaṣāya), recognize it; when it has reached equilibrium, do not disturb it.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: nāsvādayet sukhaṃ tatra niḥsaṅgaḥ prajñayā bhavet / niścalaṃ niścarac cittam ekīkuryāt prayatnataḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: One should not relish the happiness (arising there); one should be unattached through discernment; when the steady mind moves out, one should make it one with effort.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate / etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiṃcin na jāyate
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: No jīva is ever born; there is no cause for its birth. This is the highest truth, that nothing whatever is born.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

paraphrase: When one pot-space is soiled by dust and smoke, not all are; so the jīvas are not all affected by the pleasures and pains of one.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: jñānenākāśakalpena dharmān yo gaganopamān / jñeyābhinnena saṃbuddhas taṃ vande dvipadāṃ varam
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: I salute the best of men who, by knowledge like the sky and not different from its object, realized that all things (dharmas) are like the sky.
notes: Commentators differ on whom the salutation addresses (Nārāyaṇa/the supreme person per the Advaita tradition; the Buddha per some scholars). Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: durdarśam atigambhīram ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam / buddhvā padam anānātvaṃ namaskurmo yathābalam
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: Having realized that state which is hard to see, very deep, unborn, the same, pure and without multiplicity, we pay homage to it as best we can.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4.

original.text: aśaktir aparijñānaṃ kramakopo 'tha vā punaḥ / evaṃ hi sarvathā buddhair ajātiḥ paridīpitā
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: Inability (of a cause to produce), non-apprehension (of origination) and the violation of sequence (of cause and effect): in these ways non-origination has been made manifest in every way by the awakened (buddhaiḥ).
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. 'buddhaiḥ' is read by Śaṅkara as 'by the wise'; many modern readers take it as a reference to Buddhist teachers. Both readings recorded; no verdict.

paraphrase: I salute the asparśa-yoga taught (by scripture), which brings happiness and good to all beings, free from dispute and not opposed (to anyone).
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: svato vā parato vāpi na kiṃcid vastu jāyate / sad asat sadasad vāpi na kiṃcid vastu jāyate
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Nothing whatever is born, either from itself or from another; nothing whatever is born, whether existent, non-existent, or both.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: upalambhāt samācārād asti vastutvavādinām / jātis tu deśitā buddhair ajātes trasatāṃ sadā
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: Origination was taught by the awakened (buddhaiḥ) — on account of perception and of conventional practice — for those who hold that things are real and who always fear non-origination.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. A teaching of provisional instruction for those who fear the ultimate — cf. the Buddhist doctrine of skilful means; the parallel is recorded in brw:mahayana-vocabulary-in-alatasanti.

paraphrase: As a firebrand in motion appears straight, crooked and so on, so consciousness in vibration appears as perceiver and perceived.
notes: The alāta (firebrand) illustration that names the fourth prakaraṇa, Alātaśānti; 4.45–52. Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

paraphrase: We approve the non-origination proclaimed (unwittingly) by the disputants (who refute one another's theories of origination); we do not quarrel with them; learn what is beyond dispute.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.

original.text: yo 'sti kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāsty asau / paratantrābhisaṃvṛtyā syān nāsti paramārthataḥ // ajaḥ kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāpy ajaḥ / paratantrādiniṣpattyā saṃvṛtyā jāyate tu saḥ
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: What exists by imagined convention (kalpita-saṃvṛti) does not exist in the ultimate sense; what may exist by the convention of dependence on others (paratantra) does not exist ultimately. The unborn is unborn by imagined convention, not even unborn in the ultimate sense; by convention it is (said to be) born through dependence on others and the rest.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. The terms kalpita, paratantra and saṃvṛti are also the terms of the Yogācāra three natures and of the Buddhist two truths (recorded as shared vocabulary, brw:mahayana-vocabulary-in-alatasanti).

original.text: savastu sopalambhaṃ ca dvayaṃ laukikam iṣyate / avastu sopalambhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ laukikam iṣyate // avastv anupalambhaṃ ca lokottaram iti smṛtam / jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ sadā buddhaiḥ prakīrtitam
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: Duality with an object and with apprehension is held to be the worldly (laukika); apprehension without an object is the pure worldly (śuddha-laukika); without object and without apprehension is remembered as the supramundane (lokottara). Knowledge and the knowable (in these three) have always been proclaimed by the awakened.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. Three grades of cognition (waking, dream, and the state without object or apprehension); 'lokottara' is a common Buddhist term.

original.text: heyajñeyāpyapākyāni vijñeyāny agrayāṇataḥ / teṣām anyatra vijñeyād upalambhas triṣu smṛtaḥ
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: What is to be abandoned, known, attained and brought to maturity are to be understood from the foremost vehicle (agrayāna); of these, apart from the knowable (the ultimate), the other three are held to be mere apprehension.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. 'agrayāna' is otherwise a Mahāyāna self-designation; Śaṅkara glosses it as the foremost means (upāya). The construal of the second line is uncertain (moderate confidence).

original.text: alabdhāvaraṇāḥ sarve dharmāḥ prakṛtinirmalāḥ / ādau buddhās tathā muktā budhyanta iti nāyakāḥ
original.edition: GRETIL e-text 'māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikā' (via the DCS corpus), sources_raw/prepared/mandukya-karika
original.licence: Root text public domain; GRETIL e-text CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — verse-level quotation with attribution

paraphrase: All dharmas are free of any covering and pure by nature; they are awakened (buddhāḥ) and liberated from the beginning — so the leaders understand.
notes: Kārikā numbering as in the GRETIL/DCS e-text (prakaraṇa.verse), which matches the common editions for book 4. 'dharma', 'prakṛti-nirmala' and 'ādau buddhāḥ' echo Mahāyāna and Buddha-nature language; Advaita reads dharma as the selves (jīvas) identical with Brahman.

original.text: kramate na hi buddhasya jñānaṃ dharmeṣu tāyinaḥ / sarve dharmās tathā jñānaṃ naitad buddhena bhāṣitam
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The knowledge of the enlightened one, the all-pervading, does not go out to objects; all things and knowledge are likewise (unattached) — this was not spoken by the Buddha.
notes: The last line is read by the Advaita tradition as distinguishing this teaching from the Buddha's; scholars debate its sense. Kārikā numbering as in the common editions (Gambhīrānanda/Nikhilānanda); the first prakaraṇa is numbered separately from the Upaniṣad's prose.
